strategy.summary: Reproduce the stdtr/stdtrit df=-inf defect in SciPy special: on the buggy revision the isinf(df) shortcut in _cdflib_wrappers.pxd returns ndtr(t)/ndtri(p) for df=-inf, so the developer's test_stdtr_stdtrit_neg_inf fails its isnan assertions; on the fixed revision (isinf(df) and df > 0) -inf falls through to NaN handling and the test passes. The defect is a compiled-extension logic bug, so the project must be built from source at the buggy commit 44b39e1e7407 and rebuilt at the fix.

system_packages: gcc or a C/C++/Fortran toolchain capable of building SciPy
build_commands: git checkout 44b39e1e7407 && git submodule update --init && pip install -e . --no-build-isolation (or python dev.py build)
apply the developer test diff to scipy/special/tests/test_cdflib.py
git checkout <fix commit of PR 19933> and rebuild, then rerun the same test
pinned_because: numpy is documented only as a general dependency in README.rst with no version constraint, so no pin is set; a current numpy compatible with the checked-out SciPy build is chosen and stated here as a choice, not an era fact
mpmath is not a stated requirement (issue#19953 only proposes tests against it), so it is installed only as an optional aid and is not needed for the reproducing test

strategy.reproducing_test: def test_stdtr_stdtrit_neg_inf(): assert np.all(np.isnan(sp.stdtr(-np.inf, [-np.inf, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, np.inf]))); assert np.all(np.isnan(sp.stdtrit(-np.inf, [0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0])))
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 44b39e1e7407 the test FAILS: stdtr(-inf, t) returns ndtr(t) (finite values, not NaN) so np.isnan(...) is False and the first assert raises AssertionError. On the fixed revision the test PASSES: -inf falls through to the isnan handling and every stdtr/stdtrit output is NaN, so both asserts hold.
strategy.numerical_probe: sp.stdtr(-np.inf, 0.0) on buggy returns 0.5 (ndtr(0)) versus nan expected; sp.stdtrit(-np.inf, 0.5) on buggy returns ndtri(0.5)=0.0 versus nan expected.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: ndtr(t), the value from the normal distribution

risks: The defect is a branch-logic bug independent of architecture or sanitizer, so it should transition on any standard Linux x86_64 build; no special platform is required by the evidence.
The build must actually compile _cdflib_wrappers.pxd from source; testing against a wheel or a previously installed SciPy will not reproduce the buggy branch or show the fix.
Dtype and precision are not stated by the evidence; the signatures take double arguments, and the test passes Python floats via numpy, so double is assumed.
Only df=-inf is in scope; do not conflate the ncfdtrinc search bound from issue#19953 or the test_nctdtrinc_gh19896 tolerance (rtol=2e-12) with this fix.
The fix PR commit hash is not given in the context; the fixed revision must be identified from PR 19933's merge commit before the transition can be checked.
mpmath is undocumented as a requirement and is not used by the reproducing test, so its absence should not block reproduction.
The numpy version is unbounded by evidence; a very new numpy could change np.isnan on array outputs, so record the version used when reporting the result.

oracle.reference_source: the NaN result required by the commit message and PR#19933 (-inf must return nan)
oracle.why: The expected result is NaN, which is an exact predicate (np.isnan), so no numerical tolerance is needed for this test.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On buggy 44b39e1e7407, the shortcut 'if isinf(df):' catches df=-inf and returns ndtr(t) for stdtr (finite values such as 0.5 at t=0) and ndtri(p) for stdtrit. np.isnan of those finite values is False, so the first assert raises AssertionError.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the shortcut is 'if isinf(df) and df > 0:', so -inf skips the shortcut and reaches the isnan(df) check, yielding NaN for every element; both asserts hold and the test passes.
